---
title: "Initial conditions and matched modes"
---

## Specify a physical field {#sec-physical-specification}

A reproducible amplitude statement is

```text
Bcom_rms(z_reference; kmin <= k <= kmax) = value
normalization = total_band_rms | reference_band_rms
window = declared cutoff function; seed = declared integer
```

A bare "3 pG PMF" leaves the epoch, bandwidth, normalization, and realization
undefined. Direct initialization does not supply a pre-start transfer model:
`MHD_PMF_NORMALIZATION_Z` must equal `MHD_ZSTART` unless a compatible pre-evolved
state is supplied. Earlier physical normalization requires transferring density,
velocity, magnetic fields, photons, and chemistry consistently to the handoff.
{{< src "src/production/runner.jl" "pmf_normalization_z" >}}

## Batchelor initializer {#sec-batchelor}

The nonhelical Gaussian initializer constructs a random vector potential in
Fourier space and forms

$$
\widehat{\mathbf B}(\mathbf k)=i\mathbf s(\mathbf k)\times\widehat{\mathbf A}(\mathbf k),
\qquad s_j(k_j)=\frac{\sin(k_j\Delta x)}{\Delta x}.
$$ {#eq-discrete-curl}

The centered curl uses the same derivative symbol as the centered divergence
diagnostic, giving `s dot B = 0` to roundoff. A continuum/spectral curl uses
`s_j=k_j` instead and is not automatically divergence-free under the centered
grid diagnostic. The low-k magnetic **shell energy** has Batchelor slope
`E_B(k) proportional to k^4`; this is not a statement that the plotted
three-dimensional per-mode `P_B(k)` also has slope four.
{{< src "lib/MHDKernels/src/pmf.jl" "pmf_batchelor_field" >}}

`kcut` controls a smooth cutoff; `kmax` is the hard band edge. With no explicit
`kcut`, the raw runner scales it with grid Nyquist. That is useful for a
grid-scale benchmark, **not** a fixed-physical-spectrum resolution experiment.

## Lock phases and amplitudes {#sec-mode-locking}

Keep the box, physical band, seed, window, normalization, realization algorithm,
curl symbol, and lock grids fixed when refining:

- `mode_lock_n` constructs the shared low-mode realization on a fixed grid.
  The same seed without locking is insufficient when random-array traversal
  changes with the simulation grid.
- `curl_reference_n` fixes the centered derivative symbol used to generate
  shared coefficients. It must not exceed the simulation grid.
- `reference_kmax` and `reference_kcut` preserve the declared low band when
  adding ultraviolet modes. `MHD_PMF_HIGH_MODE_LOCK_N` can separately lock the
  high-band realization.
- `mode_realization="physical_hash"` keys vector-potential coefficients by
  physical Fourier indices. Shared, non-Nyquist modes in integer-related boxes
  then retain phases and polarizations. `realization_box/box` must be a positive
  integer for this construction.
- `physical_hash_zero_phase` is a deliberately altered phase ensemble, not
  another draw from the default random-phase ensemble. `fixed_mode_power`
  changes amplitude statistics and must be reported too.

Check actual Fourier coefficients in overlap bands; do not rely on matching
configuration labels alone.
{{< src "lib/MHDKernels/src/pmf.jl" "_physical_hash_vector_potential_k" >}}

## Normalization and resolution {#sec-normalization}

`total_band_rms` fixes the RMS over all generated modes. `reference_band_rms`
fixes RMS only below the reference cutoff, permitting total RMS to increase
when new UV modes are added. Renormalizing every extended band to the same
total RMS changes the shared large-scale field.

The initializer reports reference-band and total RMS separately. Record both.
`PMFSpectrumSpec` and `pmf_multiband_manifest` provide a resolution-independent
spectrum definition and minimum even grids for a set of band edges.
{{< src "lib/MHDKernels/src/pmf.jl" "PMFSpectrumSpec" >}}
{{< src "lib/MHDKernels/src/pmf.jl" "pmf_multiband_manifest" >}}

For a hard cutoff, cells per shortest magnetic wavelength are

$$
n_\lambda=\frac{2\pi N}{k_{\max}L}.
$$ {#eq-resolution}

Specify `minimum_cells_per_wavelength` with `kmax` to make this a runtime
requirement. A Nyquist mode always has two cells per wavelength, no matter how
large the grid. Quadratic Maxwell stress reaches roughly twice the magnetic
wavenumber, so resolving the magnetic wavelength alone does not establish
force convergence. A useful first science matrix targets at least 32 cells
per shortest B wavelength and 16 per shortest quadratic-force wavelength,
then measures convergence. The shipped research example's looser cutoff is
not a certificate that this criterion has been met.

::: {.callout-tip}
## Try it: compare grids without changing the physical problem
Create two copies of `examples/pmf-recombination.toml`. Keep `kcut`, `kmax`,
`mode_lock_n`, `curl_reference_n`, seed, band normalization, and physical box
identical; double only `run.n`. Adjust Gaussian smoothing cells to preserve
its physical length. Run to identical output redshifts and compare the
initial spectra, occupied mode counts, and subsequent histories before
interpreting the difference as a resolution error.
:::

## Analytic modes and phases {#sec-mode-phases}

Mode ICs are cell-centered at `x_i=(i-1/2)/N`, with phase `2*pi*kmode*x_i`.
The domain is periodic and `0 < kmode < N/2` for matched mode diagnostics.

| IC | Magnetic components | What it tests |
|---|---|---|
| `forcefree` / `circular` | `By=b*sin(phase)`, `Bz=b*cos(phase)`, `Bx=0` | Constant magnetic pressure |
| `sine` / `magpressure` | `By=b*sin(phase)`, other components zero | Quadratic density/force response at `2k` |
| `alfven_linear` | `Bx=Bguide`, `By=Bpert*sin(phase)` | Small transverse guide-field perturbation |
| `meanfield_linear` / `sv25_mode` | Oblique guide field; cosine in-plane or out-of-plane perturbation | Matched magnetosonic/Alfven reference comparisons |

The sine-mode `amplitude` convention uses peak field, while `rms` rescales
the non-force-free sine to its RMS. For a scalar sine wave, peak/RMS is
`sqrt(2)`; the circular two-component mode already has constant magnitude.
Report `MHD_PMF_SINGLE_MODE_NORMALIZATION` rather than silently converting.
{{< src "src/production/runner.jl" "_init_single_b_k!" >}}
{{< src "src/production/runner.jl" "_init_meanfield_linear_k!" >}}

The default gas starts uniform and at rest; the lattice DM begins at uniform
cell centers with zero peculiar velocity. These are controlled PMF forcing
experiments, not a general primordial adiabatic matter realization. Photon
adiabatic/comoving ICs and optional terminal momenta must be recorded. Changing
start redshift changes the pre-start history even with the same PMF seed.

## Importing a handoff {#sec-import-state}

### Generate and inspect a magnetic realization

```sh
julia --project=. -t auto scripts/generate_ic.jl \
  examples/cosmology-smoke.toml results/initial-field
```

This standalone **Batchelor magnetic-field** generator writes `bx.f32`,
`by.f32`, `bz.f32`, and `ic.toml`, including field hashes, dimensions, byte
order, normalization statistics, and source fingerprint. Arrays are Float32
in Julia column-major order with x fastest, in MHD code magnetic units at the
configured start redshift, not raw gauss or nG. It refuses a nonempty output
directory. It does not pre-evolve gas, photons, particles, or chemistry.
{{< src "scripts/generate_ic.jl" "magnetic_code_amplitude" >}}

To use the exact field at the **same epoch and units**, configure
`MHD_INITIAL_B_IMPORT_DIR` in `[environment]` with that directory. Regenerate
after changing the normalization epoch. Magnetic-only import is not a full
physical handoff and is not checkpoint resume. Use the separate Python
matched-state generators for controlled linear guide-field handoffs.

### Import a complete pre-evolved state

`MHD_INITIAL_STATE_DIR` supports the driver's explicit state import path. Treat
field names, dimensions, scalar type, storage convention, normalization epoch,
and photon/chemistry payload as a single contract. Use the parser's actual
schema rather than constructing an ad hoc file from a plot. State import is
not the same operation as [checkpoint resume](outputs.qmd#sec-restart).
{{< src "src/production/runner.jl" "initial_state_dir" >}}
